h1:
Phrae Nature Trip
Phae Muang Phi, Wiang Kosai & Waterfalls in 2 Days
intro: Phrae isn't only old teak houses and town cafes. Drive a little out of town and you'll find a completely different side of nature — both Phae Muang Phi, the strange earth pillars carved by wind and rain over millions of years, and Wiang Kosai National Park in Wang Chin district, home to the big Mae Koeng Luang waterfall and a natural mineral spring. This plan fits it all into 2 days and 1 night on a self-drive basis, and we've checked the real entry fees and opening hours for 2026 for every stop.
chips: 🪨 Phae Muang Phi million-year earth pillars

blocks.html: Phrae is a second-tier town that a lot of people just drive through on the way to Nan, missing all the good nature in the process. In reality, one province packs in both earth sculptures shaped by nature itself and the province's first national park, with a big waterfall you can swim in. This plan keeps day one easy — exploring around town and Phae Muang Phi without rushing — then saves the longer drive out to Wang Chin for the waterfalls on day two, so you're not making a long round trip in a single day.

blocks.title: Read this before you set off
blocks.html: This route works best if you drive yourself or rent a car, because Phae Muang Phi is on the edge of town while Wiang Kosai National Park is out in Wang Chin district, around 80–90 km from the town center — almost 2 hours of driving. There's no public transport that goes right to the park entrance, so if you're not driving yourself you'll need to charter a car plus driver from town.

items: Day 1 — explore around town in the morning, then drive out to Phae Muang Phi in the afternoon once the heat eases, walk the earth pillars in the late-day light, and head back to sleep in Phrae town.
Day 2 — set off early toward Wang Chin district, enter Wiang Kosai National Park, swim at Mae Koeng Waterfall, stop by the mineral spring, then drive back in the afternoon.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Phrae town, then Phae Muang Phi

blocks.html: Phae Muang Phi is in Nam Cham subdistrict, around 18 km from the center of Phrae — about 20–25 minutes to drive yourself. It's a forest park where soil and rock have been eroded by wind and rain into oddly shaped pillars and cliff faces. Entry is 20 THB for adults, 10 THB for children, and free for visitors aged 60 and over. It opens roughly 08:00–17:00. Midday sun is harsh and hot here since it's all open ground, so we'd suggest coming in the late afternoon or early evening — the walk is more comfortable and the light is much nicer.

items.activity: Start the morning in Phrae's old town — walk Khum Chao Luang and the temples inside the city wall
items.note: The morning isn't hot yet, so it's an easy time to stroll the teak houses and old temples. Grab breakfast at a local khanom jeen nam ngiao spot in town.

items.activity: Lunch in town, rest out of the midday sun
items.note: Avoid Phae Muang Phi around noon — it's open ground and the sun is brutal. Wait for it to cool down first.

items.activity: Drive out of town toward Phae Muang Phi forest park, Nam Cham subdistrict
items.note: It's around 18 km. There's a car park at the entrance — buy your ticket at the gate.

items.activity: Walk the earth pillars and cliff faces of Phae Muang Phi
items.note: There's a loop trail past the highlights, like the mushroom-shaped pillars and the 'curtain' cliff. It's an easy walk of around 45 minutes to 1 hour — wear shoes you can walk on sand in.

items.activity: Catch the evening light as the sun drops low
items.note: Late in the day the orange light hitting the earth pillars looks its best, and it's a quiet time to shoot before the crowds spread out.

items.activity: Drive back into Phrae town and check in
items.note: Sleep in town tonight to rest up properly before the long drive out to Wang Chin first thing tomorrow.

blocks.title: Tips for the Phae Muang Phi day
blocks.html: The ground is sandy soil with not much shade, so bring drinking water, a hat and sunscreen with you. In the rainy season the paths can get slippery and some sections close for safety, so check the forest park's page again before you go.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Wang Chin, Wiang Kosai National Park, Mae Koeng Waterfall

blocks.html: Wiang Kosai is the first national park in Phrae province, covering high mountain country along the Phrae–Lampang border. Its headquarters sit in Wang Chin district, around 13 km from the district town along Highway 1023, and roughly 80–90 km from the center of Phrae — about an hour and a half to nearly 2 hours' drive. The highlight is Mae Koeng Luang Waterfall, a big waterfall that tumbles down in tiers, plus Mae Koeng Noi Waterfall, which is a roughly 2 km walk from the headquarters. The park opens around 08:00–16:30.

items.activity: Check out and leave Phrae town for Wang Chin district
items.note: Fill the tank and grab breakfast to take with you, since there are few shops along the road as you head into the park.

items.activity: Arrive at Wiang Kosai National Park headquarters and pay the entry fee
items.note: The road into the park is a winding mountain road — drive slowly and watch for oncoming traffic.

items.activity: Swim at Mae Koeng Luang Waterfall
items.note: It's a big, powerful waterfall with clear cold water and pools you can wade into on some tiers. Watch for slippery rocks and read the warning signs during high-water periods.

items.activity: Break for lunch inside the park
items.note: The headquarters area has rest spots and small eateries. If you've brought your own food, you can picnic by the water.

items.activity: Short hike to Mae Koeng Noi Waterfall / stop by the mineral spring
items.note: Mae Koeng Noi is about a 2 km walk from the headquarters. If you don't want a long walk, soak in the park's mineral spring instead.

items.activity: Drive out of the park back to Phrae town
items.note: Leave before evening since the mountain road is hard to drive at night. You'll reach town around 5 pm.

blocks.title: Straight talk about the waterfall
blocks.html: Mae Koeng Luang Waterfall closes from 1 July to 31 October every year because it's the rainy season, the water runs high and it gets dangerous. If you're coming to swim, avoid this window. The waterfall is at its best with the most water from late rainy season into early winter (November–January), while in the dry season the flow drops off.

blocks.text: Want to sleep in the forest? Camping at Wiang Kosai

blocks.html: If you have more than 2 days and want to spend a night up in the mountains, Wiang Kosai has campsites and park bungalows you can book. Staying overnight means waking up to cool air and thin mist drifting through the valley — something you just don't see on a day trip out and back.

items.name: Campsites
items.blurb: There are several campsites within the park. You can rent a tent and bedding at the headquarters, or pitch your own. Best on a late-rainy-season or early-winter night.

items.name: Park bungalows
items.blurb: The park has bungalows such as the Mae Chok and Mae Koeng Noi houses. Book ahead through the national park reservation system (nps.dnp.go.th), especially over long weekends.

items.name: Mineral spring
items.blurb: The park has a natural mineral spring you can soak in to ease tired muscles — perfect after a full day of hiking or swimming at the waterfall.

items.name: Pack what you need
items.blurb: Phone signal is patchy in spots inside the park and shops are scarce, so bring cash, a flashlight, mosquito repellent and a warm layer for the night.

blocks.text: Entry fees for the key stops (updated 2026)

items: Phae Muang Phi forest park — adults 20 THB · children 10 THB · visitors aged 60+ free · open roughly 08:00–17:00
Wiang Kosai National Park — there's a park entry fee at the standard national park rates · open roughly 08:00–16:30
Mae Koeng Luang Waterfall — included in the park entry fee · closed 1 Jul–31 Oct every year
Campsites / bungalows — charged separately; book and ask at nps.dnp.go.th or call 081-030-8663

blocks.title: Treat these figures as estimates
blocks.html: Park fees and accommodation rates can change with national park policy and the season. The numbers above are based on the latest information, so it's worth calling the park to double-check before you travel — especially if you're staying overnight on a long weekend.

items.name: A car that's ready
items.blurb: The road into Wang Chin and the final stretch into the park is a winding mountain road. Check your brakes and tires beforehand, drive slowly, and use a low gear on the descents.

items.name: Swim gear
items.blurb: Mae Koeng has pools you can wade into on some tiers, so pack a change of clothes, non-slip shoes and a waterproof pouch for your phone.

items.name: Sun protection & water
items.blurb: Phae Muang Phi is open ground with harsh sun, so bring a hat, sunscreen and drinking water.

items.name: Cash
items.blurb: Park fees, accommodation and many shops in Wang Chin mostly take cash, and the signal is patchy in places.

faq.q: Can I visit Phae Muang Phi and Wiang Kosai on the same day?
faq.a: We don't recommend it. Wiang Kosai is out in Wang Chin district, around 80–90 km from Phrae town — nearly 2 hours of driving each way — while Phae Muang Phi is on the edge of town. Fitting both into one day means a lot of long-distance driving and far too much rushing. Better to split them into Day 1 (around town and Phae Muang Phi) and Day 2 (Wang Chin and the waterfall).

faq.q: How much is entry to Phae Muang Phi?
faq.a: In 2026 it's 20 THB for adults, 10 THB for children, and free for visitors aged 60 and over. The forest park opens roughly 08:00–17:00. We'd suggest coming in the late afternoon or early evening, since midday is harsh and sunny on open ground.

faq.q: When can you swim at Mae Koeng Waterfall?
faq.a: Mae Koeng Luang Waterfall closes from 1 July to 31 October every year because it's the rainy season with high water. The best time for nice water and swimming is from late rainy season into early winter, roughly November to January, when the flow is high and clear. In the dry season the water drops off.

faq.q: Can I do this plan without driving myself?
faq.a: It's pretty tough, because there's no public transport that goes right to the Wiang Kosai entrance. The easiest way is to rent a car and drive yourself, or charter a car plus driver from Phrae town. Phae Muang Phi is more doable by chartered tuk-tuk or taxi from town, since it's closer.

faq.q: How do I book a place to stay in Wiang Kosai National Park?
faq.a: The park has campsites and bungalows. Book through the national park accommodation reservation system at nps.dnp.go.th, or call the park to ask at 081-030-8663 or 093-272-7806. Book ahead, especially over long weekends and during the late-rainy-season-to-early-winter period.
